topics.title: Greetings and Forms of Address
topics.objective: Use Akan (Twi) greetings, farewells, polite expressions and respectful titles appropriate to the time of day and the person addressed.

topics.title: Alphabet and Phonetics
topics.objective: Identify the letters, special vowels, digraphs and tonal features of the Akan (Twi) writing system.

topics.title: Numbers and Counting
topics.objective: Use Akan (Twi) cardinal and ordinal numbers correctly and explain how compound numerals are built.

topics.title: Family and Kinship
topics.objective: Use Akan kinship terms correctly and describe how family membership is traced in the matrilineal system.

topics.title: Grammar and Sentence Structure
topics.objective: Identify Akan pronouns, question words, plural formation, word order and the prefixes that mark tense and negation.

topics.title: Proverbs and Idioms
topics.objective: Interpret common Akan proverbs and idioms and explain the wisdom they teach.

topics.title: Oral Literature and Culture
topics.objective: Describe Akan oral literature, day names, festivals, libation and the roles of the okyeame and talking drums.

questions.prompt: Twi is described as a tonal language. What does this mean?

options.label: A
options.text: The pitch at which a syllable is spoken can change the meaning of a word
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. In a tonal language, high and low pitch distinguish words that otherwise have the same letters — for example “papa” can mean “good” or “fan” depending on the tones. Tone is about pitch, not loudness or singing, and it is normally not written in everyday Twi spelling.

options.label: B
options.text: Every sentence must be sung to a fixed melody

options.label: C

options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the explanation established in the worked solution.

options.label: D
options.text: Words are written with musical notes
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the explanation established in the worked solution.

questions.workedSolution: In a tonal language, high and low pitch distinguish words that otherwise have the same letters — for example “papa” can mean “good” or “fan” depending on the tones. Tone is about pitch, not loudness or singing, and it is normally not written in everyday Twi spelling. Therefore the correct answer is A: The pitch at which a syllable is spoken can change the meaning of a word.
